library(tidyverse)

**NYC SUBWAY**
```{r}
# Calling the data
hw2_nyc_raw <- read.csv("data/nyc_subway_data.csv")

# Cleaning variable names
hw2_nyc_clean_names <- janitor::clean_names(hw2_nyc_raw)

# Retaining the desired variables
hw2_nyc_clean <- select(hw2_nyc_clean_names, line, station_name, station_latitude, station_longitude, route1:route11, entry, vending, entrance_type, ada)

# Changing entry from character to logical variable
library(dplyr)
hw2_nyc_clean <- hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  mutate(
    entry = case_match(
      entry,
      "YES" ~ TRUE,
      "NO" ~ FALSE,
      .default = NA
    )
  )

# Checking number of rows and columns
nrow(hw2_nyc_clean)
ncol(hw2_nyc_clean)
```

This dataset contains information about NYC subway entrances and exits, including subway line, station name, geographic coordinates, routes served, entrance type, ADA compliance, entry availability, and vending availability. To begin cleaning this data, I first created a new data frame containing only the desired variables, then converted the Entry column from a character variable (YES/NO) to a logical variable (TRUE/FALSE). The resulting dataset includes 19 columns and 1868 rows. The data are not fully tidy because the route names and numbers are currently spread across multiple columns.

```{r}
# How many distinct stations are there?
hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()

# How many stations are ADA compliant?
hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  filter(ada == "TRUE") %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()

# Proportion of entrances with entry and no vending
entry_no_vending <- 
  hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  filter(entry == TRUE, vending == "NO") %>%
  nrow()

no_vending <- 
  hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  filter(vending == "NO") %>%
  nrow()

entry_no_vending_proportion <- entry_no_vending/no_vending
entry_no_vending_proportion
```

There are 465 distinct stations in this dataset.
There are 84 stations that are ADA compliant in this dataset.
Of the entrances without vending, 37.7% allow entry.

```{r}
# Separating route name and number
hw2_nyc_clean <- hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  mutate(across(route1:route11, as.character)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = route1:route11,
    names_to = "route_number",
    names_prefix = "route",
    values_to = "route_name"
  )

# How many distinct stations serve the A train?
distinct_a_train <- hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  filter(route_name == "A") %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()

distinct_a_train

# Of the A train stations, how many are ADA compliant?
distinct_a_train_ada <- hw2_nyc_clean %>%
  filter(route_name == "A", ada == "TRUE") %>%
  distinct(line, station_name) %>%
  nrow()

distinct_a_train_ada
```

There are 60 distinct stations that serve the A train.
Of these stations serving the A train, 17 are ADA compliant.


**MR. TRASH  WHEEL**
```{r, warning = FALSE}
# Calling Mr. Trash Wheel sheet
hw2_mrtrashwheel_raw <- read_excel("data/trash_wheel_data.xlsx", sheet = "Mr. Trash Wheel", skip = 1)

# Fixing variable names
hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean <- janitor::clean_names(hw2_mrtrashwheel_raw)

# Removing non-data entries
hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean <- select(hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean, -x15, -x16)

hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean <- hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(dumpster))

# Rounding number of sports balls
hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean <- hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean %>%
  mutate(
    sports_balls = as.integer(sports_balls)
  )

# Calling Prof Trash Wheel sheet
hw2_proftrashwheel_raw <- read_excel("data/trash_wheel_data.xlsx", sheet = "Professor Trash Wheel", skip = 1)

# Fixing variable names
hw2_proftrashwheel_clean <- janitor::clean_names(hw2_proftrashwheel_raw)

# Removing non-data entries
hw2_proftrashwheel_clean <- hw2_proftrashwheel_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(dumpster))

# Calling Gwynnda sheet
hw2_gwynnda_raw <- read_excel("data/trash_wheel_data.xlsx", sheet = "Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the W", skip = 1)

# Fixing variable names
hw2_gwynnda_clean <- janitor::clean_names(hw2_gwynnda_raw)

# Removing non-data entries
hw2_gwynnda_clean <- hw2_gwynnda_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(dumpster))

# Adding a trash wheel variable to each sheet
hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean <- hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean %>%
  mutate(trash_wheel = "mister")

hw2_proftrashwheel_clean <- hw2_proftrashwheel_clean %>%
  mutate(trash_wheel = "professor")

hw2_gwynnda_clean <- hw2_gwynnda_clean %>%
  mutate(trash_wheel = "gwynnda")

# Matching variable types before combining
hw2_proftrashwheel_clean <- hw2_proftrashwheel_clean %>%
  mutate(plastic_bottles = as.numeric(plastic_bottles))

hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean <- hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean %>%
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year))

# Combining all three sheets
hw2_trash_wheels_combined <- bind_rows(
  hw2_mrtrashwheel_clean,
  hw2_proftrashwheel_clean,
  hw2_gwynnda_clean
)

# Total number of observations in combined dataset
total_obs_trashwheels <- nrow(hw2_trash_wheels_combined)
total_obs_trashwheels

# Total weight of trash collected by Professor Trash Wheel
total_weight_prof_trash <- 
  hw2_trash_wheels_combined %>%
  filter(trash_wheel == "professor") %>%
  pull(weight_tons) %>%
  sum()
total_weight_prof_trash

# Number of cigarette butts collected by Gwynnda in June 2022
gwynnda_cigs_june_2022 <-
  hw2_trash_wheels_combined %>%
  filter(trash_wheel == "gwynnda", month == "June", year == 2022) %>%
  pull(cigarette_butts) %>%
  sum()
gwynnda_cigs_june_2022
```
This dataset features data from three trash wheels, such as total weight and volume of trash collected, amounts of various types of trash collected, and dates of collection. This dataset includes a total of 1269 observations. 

The total weight of trash collected by Professor Trash Wheel in this dataset is 294.96 tons.

Gwynnda collected 18,120 cigarette butts in June of 2022. 


**ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE**
```{r, warning = FALSE}
# Calling the data
hw2_alz_baseline_raw <- read.csv("data/mci_baseline.csv", skip = 1)

# Cleaning variable names
hw2_alz_baseline_clean <- janitor::clean_names(hw2_alz_baseline_raw)

# Renaming variables
hw2_alz_baseline_clean <- hw2_alz_baseline_clean %>%
  rename(age_baseline = current_age,
         apoe4_carrier = apoe4,
         age_onset = age_at_onset)

# Replacing periods with NA
hw2_alz_baseline_clean <- hw2_alz_baseline_clean %>%
  mutate(
    age_onset = na_if(age_onset, ".")
  )

# Changing 0/1 variables to character
hw2_alz_baseline_clean <- hw2_alz_baseline_clean %>%
  mutate(
    sex = case_match(
      sex,
      1 ~ "male",
      0 ~ "female"),
    apoe4_carrier = case_match(
      apoe4_carrier,
      1 ~ "carrier",
      0 ~ "noncarrier")
  )

# Removing participants with no MCI at baseline
hw2_alz_baseline_mci_only <- hw2_alz_baseline_clean %>%
  filter(!is.na(age_onset))
```

This dataset houses information about participants in a study regarding development of Alzheimer's disease, including data such as demographic information, age of MCI onset, and APOE4 carrier status. Upon importing this dataset, it was important to clean up the variable names, rename them to be more succinct, remove the header observation row, change values encoded as 0/1 (sex and APOE4 carrier status) to character variables, and remove participants who did not develop MCI.

```{r, warning = FALSE}
# Number of recruited participants that develop MCI?
number_participants_total <- nrow(hw2_alz_baseline_clean)
number_participants_total

number_participants_mci <- nrow(hw2_alz_baseline_mci_only)
number_participants_mci

# Average baseline age
hw2_alz_baseline_clean <- hw2_alz_baseline_clean %>%
  mutate(age_baseline = as.numeric(age_baseline))

avg_baseline_age <- mean(hw2_alz_baseline_clean$age_baseline, na.rm = TRUE)
avg_baseline_age

# Percentage of women that are APOE4 carriers
women_total_alz_study <- hw2_alz_baseline_clean %>%
  filter(sex == "female") %>%
  nrow()

women_apoe4_carrier <- hw2_alz_baseline_clean %>%
  filter(sex == "female", apoe4_carrier == "carrier") %>%
  nrow()

prop_women_apoe4_carrier <- women_apoe4_carrier/women_total_alz_study
prop_women_apoe4_carrier
```

A total of 483 participants were recruited, of which 97 developed MCI.
The average baseline age is 65 years old.
Of women in the study, 29.8% are APOE4 carriers.

```{r, warning = FALSE}
# Calling the data
hw2_alz_biomarkers_raw <- read.csv("data/mci_amyloid.csv", skip = 1)

# Cleaning variable names
hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean <- janitor::clean_names(hw2_alz_biomarkers_raw)

nrow(hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean)
ncol(hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean)

# Converting variables to numeric
hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean <- hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(baseline, time_2, time_4, time_6, time_8),
      as.numeric
    )
  )
```
This dataset contains information on longitudinal biomarker values, with 6 variables and 487 observations. Biomarker values are reported at baseline and four timepoints. To clean this dataset, I removed the repetitive header row, converted variable names to snake case, and converted biomarker values from character to to numeric. 

```{r, warning = FALSE}
# Matching ID variable names
hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean <- hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean %>%
  rename(id = study_id)

# Finding participants only in the baseline dataset
hw2_baseline_only <- anti_join(
  hw2_alz_baseline_clean,
  hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean,
  by = "id"
)

nrow(hw2_baseline_only)

# Finding participants only in the amyloid dataset
hw2_amyloid_only <- anti_join(
  hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean,
  hw2_alz_baseline_clean,
  by = "id"
)

nrow(hw2_amyloid_only)

# Combining the datasets
hw2_alz_combined <- inner_join(
  hw2_alz_baseline_clean,
  hw2_alz_biomarkers_clean,
  by = "id"
)

nrow(hw2_alz_combined)
ncol(hw2_alz_combined)
```
There are 8 participants who only appear in the baseline group, and 12 participants who only appear in the amyloid group. The combined dataset includes only participants who have baseline and amyloid biomarker data. This combined dataset includes 11 variables and 475 observations, providing information on participants' baseline characteristics and biomarker values over time. 

```{r, warning = FALSE}
# Exporting the dataset as CSV
write.csv(
  hw2_alz_combined,
  "data/hw2_alz_combined.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
